extraction_text: Stanu has eleven famous sons born from his highest thought.
Angiras has three sons: Brihaspati, Utathya, and Samvartana.
Atri has many sons who are great sages.
Pulastya's descendants are Rakshasas, monkeys, and Kinnaras.
Pulaha's descendants are deer, lions, tigers, and Kimpurushas.
Kratu's sons are identical to him and are companions of the sun.
Sage Daksha is born from Brahma's right thumb.
Daksha's wife is born from Brahma's left thumb.
Daksha fathers fifty daughters with his wife.
Daksha gives ten daughters to Dharma, twenty-seven to Chandra, and thirteen to Kashyapa.
Dharma's ten wives are named: Kirti, Lakshmi, Dhriti, Medha, Pushti, Shraddha, Kriya, Buddhi, Lajja, and Mati.
Chandra's twenty-seven wives are the Nakshatras (lunar mansions).
The progenitor has a son who is a Prajapati, and this Prajapati has eight sons known as the Vasus.
The eight Vasus are named: Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Aha, Anila, Anala, Pratyusha, and Prabhasa.
Dhara and Dhruva are sons of Tumula, Soma is son of Manasvini, and Anila is son of Shvasa.
Genealogical descriptions of divine beings and their offspring.
Aha (Day) is the son of Ratha.
Agni (Fire God) is the son of Samlili.
Pratyusha (Dawn) and Prabhasa (Light) are known as the two sons of Prabhata.
Dhruva (Pole Star) has a son, the venerable Kala (Time), who drives the worlds.
Soma (Moon God) has a son, the radiant Varchas (Splendor).
Varchas (Splendor) and Manohara (Fascination) gave birth to Shishira, Prana, and later Ramana.
Aha (Day) has sons: Jyoti (Radiance), Shrama (Toil), Shanta (Peace), and Muni (Sage).
Agni (Fire God) has a son, the very auspicious Kumara (Youth), whose abode is the reed thicket.
Agni (Fire God) also has sons Shakha and Vishakha, and later Nigamisha was born.
Anila (Wind God)'s wife is Shiva, and her sons are Pulojava and Abhijatakati.
Pratyusha (Dawn) has a son, the sage Devala.
Devala has two sons, generous and wise.
Brihaspati (Lord of Speech) has a sister, a beautiful woman who practiced asceticism, achieved yogic powers, and roamed the universe unhindered.
She is the wife of the eighth Vasu, Vasuprabhasa (Light).

She gave birth to the greatly fortunate Vishvakarma, the progenitor of crafts, creator of thousands of arts, carpenter of the thirty-three gods, creator of all ornaments, and maker of the gods' magical flying chariots.

attributes.divine_element: Creation of divine crafts and vehicles

extraction_text: The venerable Dharma was born from Brahma's right breast in human form, bringing happiness to the world.
Dharma has three excellent sons who captivate all beings: Shama (Peace), Kama (Love), and Harsha (Joy) who supports the world with divine light.
Kama (Love God)'s wife is Rati (Desire), Shama (Peace)'s wife is Prabhavati (Achievement), and Harsha (Joy)'s wife is Nandi (Delight).
Kashyapa is the son of Marichi, and both Devas (Gods) and Asuras (Demons) are born from Kashyapa, who is the origin of all worlds.
Tvashtri is the wife of Savita, and in the form of a mare in the sky, she gave birth to the Ashvins.
Aditi has twelve sons, led by Indra, with Vishnu being the last born, through whom all worlds exist.
These gods are called the 'Thirty-Three Gods', and their descendants and groups are described according to their lineages and families.
Rudra, Sadhya, Maruts, and Vasus have separate lineages.
Bhrigu was born after splitting Brahma's heart.
Bhrigu's son was the learned Kavi.
Kavi's son was Shukra (Venus), a planet.
Shukra was appointed by Ishvara (Brahma) to oversee the welfare of all beings in the three worlds, managing rain, drought, terror, and peace, and to orbit the world.
Shukra was a yoga master, highly intelligent, teacher of both Daityas and Suras (gods), knowledgeable, practicing celibacy, and self-restrained.
After Shukra was appointed by Vishnu (Brahma) to oversee human welfare, Bhrigu had another flawless son, Chyavana.
Chyavana had great ascetic power, was righteous, wise, and fell from the womb due to impatience to be born.

supernatural_elements: Fell from womb due to impatience

extraction_text: Manu's daughter Arushi was the wife of wise Chyavana.

attributes.relationship: Marriage (Arushi and Chyavana), Father-Daughter (Manu and Arushi)

extraction_text: Urja (also known as Aurva) was born by splitting the thigh, had great ascetic power, radiant, and possessed virtues even as a child.
Richika was the son of Urja (Aurva), and later had a son named Jamadagni.
Jamadagni had four noble sons, with Rama (Parashurama) being the youngest, skilled in weapons and divine missiles, and the leader in exterminating Kshatriyas.
Before Jamadagni, Urja (Aurva) had a hundred sons, who in turn had thousands of sons, all descendants of Bhrigu.
Brahma had two other sons, Dhatri (Sustainer) and Vidhatri (Creator), whose forms remain in the world, and they are with Manu.
Their sister was the goddess Lakshmi (Goddess of Fortune), dwelling in red lotuses, incomparably radiant, and her mind-born sons were celestial horses that travel through the sky.
Varuna's wife Jyeshtha (Eldest), a goddess born from Shukra, gave birth to sons Bala and the divine Sura (celestial liquor) beloved by gods.
From beings craving food and devouring each other, Adharma (Unrighteousness) was born, the destroyer of all beings.
Adharma's wife was Nirriti, and from her were born Rakshasas, and three evil sons: Bhaya (Terror), Mahabhaya (Great Terror), and Mrityu (Death) who causes beings to perish.
The goddess Tamra gave birth to five famous daughters: Kaki (female crow), Shyeni (female hawk), Bhasi (female vulture), Dhritarashtra (female goose), and Shuki (female parrot).

supernatural_elements: Goddess giving birth to bird forms
